transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. transcript.text: Mara, I need to flag a rights issue with 'After the Floodlights.' I reviewed the executed music and archive license this morning, and there are three key constraints: (1) the festival may hold exactly one in-person public screening — so the planned screening is fine, but no additional screenings can be added; (2) we may NOT publish any trailer or excerpt online, which conflicts with the draft program's planned online trailer; and (3) we must use the exact credit 'Courtesy of Northline Archive.' I also want to note that I haven't added the license summary to the programming file yet because the signed copy arrived in my separate clearance inbox, so the team wouldn't have seen this information there.

transcript.text: Mara, I need to flag a premiere-status issue with 'After the Floodlights.' I checked the filmmaker's signed premiere declaration against the festival database today and confirmed that the film already had a public screening at the Harbor Documentary Week. That means it fails the competition's unpublished-premiere requirement, so it cannot remain in the official competition. If we retain it at all, it would need to be offered as a single special screening instead. I should also note that I haven't updated the submission record yet because the database correction queue is still open, so this issue wouldn't be visible in the system to the rest of the team.

transcript.text: Thank you both, Jonas and Leila. These are exactly the kinds of issues I needed to hear about before locking the program. Given both issues, I'm inclined to remove it from competition and offer it as a single special screening — one in-person screening only, no online trailer, with the required credit. Let me make the final decision now.

transcript.text: Mara, I support your proposed decision. From a rights clearance standpoint, a single in-person special screening with no online trailer and the exact credit 'Courtesy of Northline Archive' would fully comply with the license terms I reviewed this morning. I'll make sure the license summary gets added to the programming file promptly so the team has it on record. transcript.text: Thank you, Mara. I support the decision as well.
